items.q: Match the following cause of CKD with its rate of fall of GFR (ml/min/year) — 1) DKD  2) CGN  3) IN  4) CTID … A) 4-6  B) 8-10  C) 2-4  D) 6-8
items.exp: Table: rate of fall of GFR (ml/min/year) — DKD 8-10; CGN 6-8; IN 4-6; CTID 2-4. (Book p806)

items.q: The rate of fall of GFR listed for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is:
The rate of fall of GFR listed for ischemic nephropathy (IN) is:
In the complications row of the causes table, which two columns carry the ↑↑ marks?
items.exp: Complications row: DKD — ↑↑ vascular complications; IN — ↑↑ macrovascular complications; CGN and CTID are marked '-'. (Book p806)

items.q: CGN shows ↑↑ macrovascular complications in the causes table.
opts: False — the CGN column is marked '-'; macrovascular is under IN
items.exp: Complications row: CGN '-', IN ↑↑ macrovascular complications. (Book p806)

items.q: A CKD patient with a long history of atheromatous vascular disease is losing GFR at about 5 ml/min/year. Which causes-column fits best?
items.exp: IN column: rate 4-6 ml/min/year and ↑↑ macrovascular complications. (Book p806)

items.q: The slowest rate of fall of GFR in the causes table, 2-4 ml/min/year, belongs to:
